title: Madras HC: NGT Has No Jurisdiction Over Coastal Aquaculture Licensing Disputes
case_name: M/s Golden Marine Harvest v. National Green Tribunal
card_summary: The NGT's Southern Zone bench had ordered closure of several shrimp hatcheries for lacking Coastal Regulation Zone clearance. The Madras High Court quashed the order, holding the Coastal Aquaculture Authority Act, 2005 is not among the statutes listed in the NGT Act's schedule, so the Tribunal had no jurisdiction over such units under it. The Bench separately opened a suo motu writ on CRZ compliance.
card_tip: A coastal aquaculture business facing an NGT closure order should first check the Tribunal's jurisdiction; the Coastal Aquaculture Authority Act's absence from the NGT Act's schedule is a standing objection.
verification_notes: Parties, citation (2026 MHC 1814), the Southern Zone NGT closure order, the jurisdictional holding on the CAA Act's exclusion from the NGT Act's schedule, and the suo motu writ on CRZ compliance are reported consistently by Verdictum, with the jurisdictional point also summarised by GKToday and TNPSC Thervupettagam. The suo motu proceeding was still pending as of the sources reviewed.
